title: Eighth Word Applying The Symbols In The Comparison General Principle

questions.question: What choice is the listener being urged to make at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: To avoid being like the unlucky brother and instead be like the blessed brother.

questions.question: What two things is the listener told to do with the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Listen to it and obey what it commands.

questions.question: If someone understands the comparison, what will that person be able to connect it to?
questions.answer: The truths about religion, the world, human beings, and belief in Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage explain every small detail, or mainly the most important ones?
questions.answer: It mainly explains the most important ones.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the two brothers in the explanation?
questions.answer: One stands for a believing, upright inner self, and the other stands for an unbelieving, corrupt inner self.

questions.question: What does the road on the right stand for?
questions.answer: The path of the Qur’an and faith in Allah.

questions.question: What does the road on the left stand for?
questions.answer: The path of disobedience and denial.

questions.question: In this explanation, what does the garden on the road represent?
questions.answer: A person’s short life in human society and civilization.

questions.question: Why does the garden include both pleasant and unpleasant things?
questions.answer: Because life in this world has good and bad mixed together.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a wise person do when faced with mixed things?
questions.answer: He takes what is pure and beneficial and leaves what is troubling and dirty.

questions.question: What result comes from choosing the good and leaving the bad?
questions.answer: A calm and peaceful heart.

questions.question: What does the desert symbolize?
questions.answer: The earth and this worldly life.

questions.question: What does the lion symbolize?
questions.answer: Death and a person’s fixed time to die.

questions.question: What does the well stand for?
questions.answer: The human body and the span of a person’s life.

questions.question: What does the well’s depth point to?
questions.answer: A usual lifetime of about sixty years.

questions.question: What does the tree growing in the well represent?
questions.answer: The period of life and what life is made of.

questions.question: Who do the white and black animals stand for?
questions.answer: Day and night.

questions.question: What does the dragon represent?
questions.answer: The way to the world after death and the place between this life and the hereafter.

questions.question: For a believer, what does the dragon’s mouth become like?
questions.answer: A doorway leading from a prison to a garden.

questions.question: What do the poisonous creatures stand for?
questions.answer: The troubles and hardships of this world.

questions.question: How are those hardships described for a believer?
questions.answer: As kind warnings and merciful gifts from Allah that wake a person up from carelessness.

questions.question: What do the fruits on the tree represent?
questions.answer: The blessings of this world.

questions.question: How are those worldly blessings connected to the hereafter?
questions.answer: They point to blessings in the next life, serve as examples and reminders, and invite people toward Paradise.

questions.question: What does the tree’s many different fruits show about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It shows a special mark of His power and rule, because only Allah can bring many things from one thing and unite many things in one.

questions.question: What is the talisman explained to be?
questions.answer: The secret of why creation was made.

questions.question: Through what is that secret solved?
questions.answer: Through the truth of faith.

questions.question: What is the key to that secret?
questions.answer: The declaration that only Allah is God, and that Allah is the Ever-Living and the Self-Subsisting.

questions.question: What does the grave mean for people who reject guidance?
questions.answer: A lonely and painful entrance like a narrow prison.

questions.question: What does the grave mean for people of faith and the Qur’an?
questions.answer: A door from this world to everlasting life and the gardens of Paradise.

questions.question: How is death described for people who are misguided?
questions.answer: As a bitter separation and a lonely entrance into the grave.

questions.question: How is death described for people of guidance?
questions.answer: As a reunion with loved ones, a return to their true home, and a rest after life’s duties.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, who is being addressed along with the nafs?
questions.answer: The person listening to the story.

questions.question: What kind of life example is the listener told not to follow?
questions.answer: The example of the unfortunate brother.

questions.question: What kind of life example is the listener told to follow?
questions.answer: The example of the fortunate brother.

questions.question: What attitude toward the Qur’an is commanded first?
questions.answer: Paying careful attention to it.

questions.question: What shows that real belief is more than hearing words?
questions.answer: The passage says to obey, hold fast, and act by the Qur’an.

questions.question: After understanding the comparison, what four big areas can a person understand better?
questions.answer: Religion, the world, human life, and faith in Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage say only the important points will be given?
questions.answer: Because the reader is expected to think and work out the smaller details too.

questions.question: What does the believing brother represent inside a person?
questions.answer: A faithful soul and a sound heart.

questions.question: What does the other brother represent inside a person?
questions.answer: A faithless soul and a spoiled heart.

questions.question: What does the right-hand road teach about life?
questions.answer: It teaches the way of faith and Qur’anic guidance.

questions.question: What does the left-hand road teach about life?
questions.answer: It teaches rebellion against truth and denial of faith.

questions.question: What part of ordinary human life is pictured by the garden?
questions.answer: Daily life among people, where clean and unclean things are together.

questions.question: What rule is given for dealing with the mixed nature of life?
questions.answer: Choose what is wholesome and leave what is muddy and upsetting.

questions.question: What reward comes from living by that rule?
questions.answer: Inner peace.

questions.question: Why does the desert fit as a picture of the world?
questions.answer: Because the passage uses it to represent the earth and worldly life as a place people travel through.

questions.question: What two realities are represented by the lion?
questions.answer: Death and the time fixed for it.

questions.question: What two things are represented by the well?
questions.answer: A person’s body and the length of his life.

questions.question: Why is the number sixty mentioned?
questions.answer: It points to an average human lifetime.

questions.question: What does the tree tell us about life?
questions.answer: It stands for life’s duration and living substance.

questions.question: Why are there two animals at the roots?
questions.answer: They symbolize the passing of day and night, which wear away life.

questions.question: What future stage is shown by the dragon?
questions.answer: The passage to the next world and the realm after death.

questions.question: How is the dragon different for a believer?
questions.answer: Its frightening opening becomes a way into beauty and safety.

questions.question: What do the harmful creatures around a person stand for in daily life?
questions.answer: Worldly problems and suffering.

questions.question: In a believer’s life, what good purpose can suffering serve?
questions.answer: It can warn and awaken the person so he does not become heedless.

questions.question: What do the fruits teach about blessings in this world?
questions.answer: They are signs and small samples pointing to greater blessings in the next world.

questions.question: Why is one tree bearing many kinds of fruit important in the explanation?
questions.answer: It shows Allah’s unique power and lordship.

questions.question: What does the passage say only Allah can do with one and many?
questions.answer: He can bring many things out of one thing and make many different things into one ordered whole.

questions.question: What is the hidden mystery called in the passage?
questions.answer: The secret purpose behind creation.

questions.question: What opens that mystery?
questions.answer: Faith, especially the testimony of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the grave for people who oppose guidance?
questions.answer: As a painful and confining entrance filled with loneliness.

questions.question: How does it describe the grave for believers?
questions.answer: As a passage into lasting life, mercy, and Paradise.

questions.question: What final comfort does the passage give about death for believers?
questions.answer: It is not only an end but also a reunion, a reward, and a rest.

questions.question: What other instruction follows listening to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: To carry out its commands.

questions.question: What shows that faith should affect a person’s actions?
questions.answer: The passage says to live in line with the Qur’an, not just know about it.

questions.question: What can the story help a person understand besides religion?
questions.answer: It can also help him understand the world, human beings, and belief in Allah.

questions.question: What is the reader expected to do with the finer details?
questions.answer: Figure them out by thinking after the main points are given.

questions.question: In the explained meaning, what does the first brother symbolize?
questions.answer: A heart and soul shaped by faith.

questions.question: What does the second, negative brother symbolize?
questions.answer: A heart and soul ruined by unbelief.

questions.question: Which road matches faith?
questions.answer: The road on the right.

questions.question: Which road matches denial and disobedience?
questions.answer: The road on the left.

questions.question: What part of human experience does the garden symbolize?
questions.answer: Life in this world among other people.

questions.question: Why is the garden not all clean and beautiful?
questions.answer: Because worldly life includes both good things and bad things.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the wise way to deal with this mixture?
questions.answer: Take the clean and pleasant part, and leave the disturbing part.

questions.question: What emotional result comes from that wise choice?
questions.answer: Peace in the heart.

questions.question: What does the desert represent in the symbolic explanation?
questions.answer: The earth and worldly existence.

questions.question: Why is the lion a fitting symbol in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it represents the frightening reality of death and the moment appointed for it.

questions.question: What does the well teach about human life?
questions.answer: That life is tied to the body and limited in length.

questions.question: What is suggested by saying the well is sixty yards deep?
questions.answer: That human life usually has a set and limited number of years.

questions.question: What does the tree in the well stand for?
questions.answer: A person’s life course and living support.

questions.question: What do the two root-cutting animals teach about time?
questions.answer: That day and night keep using up a person’s life.

questions.question: What does the dragon show about what comes after this life?
questions.answer: It points to the next stage after death.

questions.question: How does belief change the meaning of that frightening image?
questions.answer: For the believer, it turns into an entrance to a better place.

questions.question: What are the poisonous creatures around the person like in real life?
questions.answer: They are like troubles and disasters people face in the world.

questions.question: What mercy can be hidden inside troubles for a believer?
questions.answer: They can remind him of Allah and keep him spiritually awake.

questions.question: What are worldly blessings compared to in relation to the next life?
questions.answer: Signs, examples, and samples of what is prepared in the hereafter.

questions.question: What does the one tree with many fruits prove in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s unmatched power and control.

questions.question: What great truth is shown by making many things from one source?
questions.answer: That such power belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: What is the talisman in the explanation?
questions.answer: The hidden purpose behind creation.

questions.question: What phrases are named as the key?
questions.answer: The words declaring Allah’s oneness and His everlasting life and self-subsistence.

questions.question: For those who reject truth, what is the grave like?
questions.answer: A bleak and crushing place of confinement.

questions.question: For believers, what is the grave like?
questions.answer: A doorway from the prison of this world to eternal gardens.

questions.question: According to the passage, what else does death become for people of guidance?
questions.answer: A meeting with loved ones, an entrance to their real home, and relief from the burdens of worldly duty.

questions.question: What is the passage trying to help the listener avoid becoming?
questions.answer: The miserable brother.

questions.question: What is the passage trying to help the listener become instead?
questions.answer: The fortunate brother.

questions.question: What three responses to the Qur’an are required?
questions.answer: To hear it, obey it, and live by it faithfully.

questions.question: What does this show about true guidance?
questions.answer: It must shape both belief and behavior.

questions.question: What can someone understand after grasping the comparison?
questions.answer: Important truths about faith, life, people, and the world.

questions.question: Why are only the major meanings listed?
questions.answer: So the reader can reflect and discover the smaller meanings on his own.

questions.question: In the symbolic explanation, what kind of inner life does the fortunate brother represent?
questions.answer: A faithful spirit and a good heart.

questions.question: What kind of inner life does the unfortunate brother represent?
questions.answer: A faithless spirit and a corrupted heart.

questions.question: What does the right road teach a person to follow?
questions.answer: The guidance of the Qur’an and faith in Allah.

questions.question: What does the left road teach a person to follow?
questions.answer: Rebellion and rejection of truth.

questions.question: What does the garden tell us about life in society?
questions.answer: It contains both beneficial things and harmful or dirty things.

questions.question: What is the wise rule for walking through such a garden?
questions.answer: Choose the pure and beneficial things and leave the troubling ones.

questions.question: What blessing comes from using that rule?
questions.answer: Calmness of heart.

questions.question: What does the desert represent in the explanation?
questions.answer: This earth and the life of this world.

questions.question: What does the lion stand for in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: Death and the time Allah has set for it.

questions.question: What does the well stand for?
questions.answer: The human body and the period of one’s life.

questions.question: What meaning is attached to the number sixty?
questions.answer: It points to a normal human lifespan.

questions.question: What does the tree growing there represent?
questions.answer: Life’s duration and the support of living.

questions.question: What do the black and white animals represent?
questions.answer: The passing of night and day.

questions.question: What lesson can we infer from day and night gnawing at the roots?
questions.answer: Time is slowly reducing a person’s life.

questions.question: What does the dragon symbolize?
questions.answer: The passage into the next stage after death.

questions.question: For believers, how is that passage changed?
questions.answer: It becomes an opening to beauty, safety, and the hereafter.

questions.question: What do the poisonous creatures symbolize?
questions.answer: The pains and tests of worldly life.

questions.question: How can these painful things actually help a believer?
questions.answer: They can serve as gentle warnings from Allah and keep him from spiritual laziness.

questions.question: What are the fruits symbols of?
questions.answer: The blessings of worldly life.

questions.question: What three jobs do these blessings do in relation to Paradise?
questions.answer: They act as reminders, small examples, and invitations toward its blessings.

questions.question: Why is the many-fruited tree a sign of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: Because only Allah can produce great variety from one source and unite many things in one design.

questions.question: What is meant by the talisman?
questions.answer: The hidden wisdom of why creation exists.

questions.question: What unlocks that wisdom?
questions.answer: Belief, especially the words affirming Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How is the grave described for people who reject guidance?
questions.answer: As a lonely and painful gate into tight darkness.

questions.question: How is the grave described for people of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: As a gate from this world’s prison into eternal life and Paradise.

questions.question: Give two good meanings of death for believers from the passage.
questions.answer: It brings reunion with loved ones and rest from the hardships and duties of worldly life.

questions.question: Who is the advice meant for at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The speaker’s nafs and the person listening.

questions.question: What bad example should the listener stay away from?
questions.answer: The example of the unfortunate brother.

questions.question: What good example should the listener try to follow?
questions.answer: The example of the fortunate brother.

questions.question: What four actions or attitudes toward revelation are taught at the beginning?
questions.answer: Listen, obey, hold to it, and act by it.

questions.question: After understanding the story’s lesson, what kinds of truths can a person relate it to?
questions.answer: Truths about religion, this world, human life, and faith in Allah.

questions.question: What is the role of the reader after the main points are given?
questions.answer: To work out the smaller meanings by himself.

questions.question: What does the blessed brother stand for?
questions.answer: A believing inner self and a righteous heart.

questions.question: What does the unlucky brother stand for?
questions.answer: An unbelieving inner self and a corrupted heart.

questions.question: What does the right road represent?
questions.answer: The way of the Qur’an and belief.

questions.question: What does the left road represent?
questions.answer: The way of denial and rebellion.

questions.question: What does the roadside garden stand for?
questions.answer: A person’s short worldly life in society and civilization.

questions.question: What important truth about life is shown by the garden having both clean and dirty things?
questions.answer: Worldly life contains both good and bad together.

questions.question: What is the sensible person’s rule for dealing with that mixture?
questions.answer: To take what is clear and good and leave what is muddy and upsetting.

questions.question: What kind of heart does that wise approach lead to?
questions.answer: A tranquil heart.

questions.question: What does the desert symbolize?
questions.answer: The world and the earth.

questions.question: What does the lion symbolize?
questions.answer: Death and the time fixed for it.

questions.question: What does the well symbolize?
questions.answer: The body and the length of life.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention sixty years?
questions.answer: To point to the ordinary length of a human life.

questions.question: What does the tree symbolize?
questions.answer: The lifetime itself and the support of life.

questions.question: What do the white and black creatures symbolize?
questions.answer: Day and night.

questions.question: What does the dragon symbolize?
questions.answer: The path to the life after death and the intermediate state.

questions.question: What does the dragon’s mouth become for the believer?
questions.answer: A doorway from confinement to a garden.

questions.question: What do the poisonous creatures around the person symbolize?
questions.answer: The troubles and disasters of worldly life.

questions.question: What merciful purpose can those troubles have for a believer?
questions.answer: They can wake him up and keep him from heedlessness.

questions.question: What do the fruits symbolize?
questions.answer: The blessings of this world.

questions.question: How do those fruits point beyond this world?
questions.answer: They are signs and samples of the blessings of the hereafter and invitations toward Paradise.

questions.question: What does the tree having many fruits show about Allah?
questions.answer: His power, lordship, and sovereignty are unique and beyond imitation.

questions.question: What is the talisman in the passage’s explanation?
questions.answer: The secret of why creation was made.

questions.question: What is the key to solving that secret?
questions.answer: The testimony that Allah alone is God, and that He is the Ever-Living and Self-Subsisting.

questions.question: How is the grave different for people of misguidance and people of faith?
questions.answer: For the misguided it is a painful, narrow entrance, but for believers it is an opening to everlasting life and Paradise.

questions.question: How is death different for people of misguidance and people of guidance?
questions.answer: For the misguided it is a bitter separation, but for believers it is reunion, reward, and relief.

questions.question: What does the passage say death gives after the duties of life are over for believers?
questions.answer: Rest from hardship and release from the testing and worship duties of this world.

questions.question: What warning and hope are both given in the first sentence of the passage?
questions.answer: A warning not to live like the unfortunate brother, and hope to become like the fortunate brother.

questions.question: What is the first source of guidance the listener is told to turn to?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how to respond to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: A person should hear it, obey it, stay attached to it, and practice it.

questions.question: What does this tell us about real religious understanding?
questions.answer: It should lead to action, not just ideas.

questions.question: What can be understood better when the comparison is understood well?
questions.answer: The truths about religion, the world, humanity, and belief in Allah.

questions.question: Why are only key meanings explained directly?
questions.answer: Because the smaller meanings are left for the reader to infer.

questions.question: In this explanation, what does one brother represent spiritually?
questions.answer: A believing soul and upright heart.

questions.question: What does the other brother represent spiritually?
questions.answer: A disbelieving soul and ruined heart.

questions.question: What path does the right road symbolize?
questions.answer: The path of the Qur’an and faith.

questions.question: What path does the left road symbolize?
questions.answer: The path of rejecting and disobeying truth.

questions.question: What does the garden symbolize about ordinary life?
questions.answer: Human life in society where opposites are mixed together.

questions.question: What opposites are mixed together in that garden?
questions.answer: Good and evil, and clean and dirty things.

questions.question: What is the wise person’s method in such a world?
questions.answer: To choose what is wholesome and leave what harms the heart.

questions.question: What benefit comes from that method?
questions.answer: Peacefulness inside.

questions.question: What larger place does the desert symbolize?
questions.answer: The earth and this passing world.

questions.question: What does the lion remind the reader of?
questions.answer: Death and the time set for it.

questions.question: What two parts of human existence are symbolized by the well?
questions.answer: The body and the span of life.

questions.question: What does the depth of the well point toward?
questions.answer: The usual measure of a human lifetime.

questions.question: What does the tree represent?
questions.answer: Life’s period and life’s support.

questions.question: What do the two animals chewing at the roots represent?
questions.answer: Night and day.

questions.question: What can a student infer from night and day wearing down the roots?
questions.answer: Time keeps moving and life keeps getting shorter.

questions.question: What does the dragon stand for?
questions.answer: The way into the world after death.

questions.question: What does that frightening image become for a believer?
questions.answer: A doorway into a garden instead of a terrifying trap.

questions.question: What do the poisonous vermin stand for?
questions.answer: Hardships and disasters in worldly life.

questions.question: How can worldly hardships be a favor for a believer?
questions.answer: They can warn him kindly and keep him from forgetting Allah.

questions.question: What do the fruits on the tree stand for?
questions.answer: The blessings found in this world.

questions.question: How do those blessings teach about the next life?
questions.answer: They are reminders, examples, and samples of the blessings waiting in Paradise.

questions.question: Why is one tree carrying many kinds of fruit a powerful sign?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s unique ability to bring great variety from one source and perfect order from many things.

questions.question: What is the talisman said to be?
questions.answer: The hidden purpose and meaning of creation.

questions.question: What is the key that opens it?
questions.answer: Affirming Allah’s oneness and His perfect life and self-subsistence.

questions.question: What is the grave like for those who go against guidance?
questions.answer: A lonely, painful, and tight place.

questions.question: What is the grave like for those who follow the Qur’an?
questions.answer: A gate from this world’s prison to immortality, mercy, and Paradise.

questions.question: What three hopeful meanings does death have for believers in this passage?
questions.answer: It joins them with loved ones, takes them to their real home, and gives them rest and reward.
